Novelty: 2
Justification: The solution outlines a standard multi-market localization strategy (centralized core with localized content layers). While it correctly identifies the need to balance a shared technology core with local fit, it does not introduce any groundbreaking or particularly innovative approaches to adaptive learning localization that would distinguish it from conventional EdTech expansion models. 

Usefulness: 1
Justification: The solution is fundamentally impractical because it is incomplete. The text cuts off mid-sentence in the opening "Parameter note" ("Curriculum frameworks, data-residency rules, procurement thresholds and appro..."). It provides absolutely no actionable product strategy, technical architecture, or go-to-market plan. A decision-maker cannot use this text to drive any implementation.

Flexibility: 1
Justification: Because the solution is truncated and contains no actual strategy, it offers no perspectives, alternatives, or approaches. It represents zero flexibility due to the complete absence of substantive content.

Elaboration: 1
Justification: The solution is entirely undeveloped. It consists only of a title, a list of target countries, and an incomplete introductory sentence. There is no framework, no detail, and no elaboration on how to handle the specified constraints (curricula, parental attitudes, procurement channels).

Cultural Sensitivity: 2
Justification: The solution demonstrates limited awareness simply by acknowledging the target countries and listing "curriculum frameworks" and "data-residency rules" as parameters to consider. However, because it does not actually discuss cultural beliefs, screen time attitudes, or educational norms, it cannot score higher on actual cultural mindfulness.
